articles.title: Union Street roadworks in Rochdale to begin on 17 November 2026
articles.excerpt: Temporary road closure on Union Street will affect traffic from 17 November 2026, with no waiting allowed during the works.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has announced that roadworks on Union Street will commence on 17 November 2026.

The works will involve a temporary closure of part of Union Street, specifically 17 metres south of the junction with St Mary's Gate, extending to the northern side of the junction with South Lane.

The closure will begin at 7pm on Tuesday, 17 November 2026, and is expected to last until 4am on Wednesday, 18 November 2026. During this time, no waiting will be permitted in the affected section of the road, which may impact local traffic and access.

Motorists and residents should plan their journeys accordingly, as the closure will affect access to St Mary's Gate and Hunters Lane. Drivers are encouraged to check for updates on roadworks across Greater Manchester for any further restrictions or changes.

This development is significant for local commuters and residents, as it may lead to increased traffic congestion in surrounding areas. For more information and to view a map of the roadworks, visit the Rochdale Borough Council website.

articles.title: Rochdale Asda worker's kindness a 'breath of fresh air' for widowed customer
articles.excerpt: Shaheda times her help around an older customer's shopping trips after the woman lost her husband, scanning and packing her shopping and stopping for a chat.
articles.content_html:
A worker at Asda's Rochdale store has been praised for looking out for an older customer after the woman was widowed.

Shaheda first noticed something had changed when the customer, who used to shop with her husband, stopped coming in for a while. When she next saw her, the woman was shopping with her daughter, and the pair told her what had happened.

The daughter lives in London and was worried about how her mother would cope on her own. Shaheda promised to look after her and told her which days she works, so the customer could time her visits for when Shaheda would be there.

Now, when the customer comes in, Shaheda scans and packs her shopping, fetches her a chair and makes time for a chat.

The customer told the store's customer manager, Dave, how much the help meant to her. Dave said: "The lady told me that ever since she lost her husband three months ago, Shaheda has been like a breath of fresh air in her life every time she shops – not just because of the help she offers, but as an emotional support and somebody to chat to."

Shaheda said: "I used to see the lady come in with her husband all the time and then didn't see her for a while. Then I saw her shopping with her daughter, and they told me what had happened. I told her to come and see me every time she came in... and she does. We have a good chat and I help her, as she does struggle a bit."

She added: "She thanks me every single time and I go, 'no, you don't need to thank me'. It's sweet, though. I like to think that somebody would do that for my own mum. I always think too that one day I could be in that position. It doesn't cost anything to be pleasant and kind, does it?"

For someone adjusting to life alone after a bereavement, a familiar face on a weekly errand can make a real difference, and the help Shaheda gives costs nothing but a little time.

articles.title: Child taken to hospital after medical emergency at Cosy Toes nursery in Middleton
articles.excerpt: Emergency services, including an air ambulance, responded to a medical emergency involving a child at Cosy Toes nursery in Middleton on Monday afternoon.
articles.content_html:
A child has been taken to hospital following a medical emergency at Cosy Toes nursery in Middleton. Emergency services, including an air ambulance, were called to the scene at around 3.50pm on Monday, November 2, 2026.

The incident occurred at the nursery located at the junction of Mainway East and Greengate Road. Witnesses reported a significant emergency response, with three police vehicles, an ambulance, and a rapid response paramedic car present.

The air ambulance landed on a nearby grass verge to assist.

A spokesperson for Greater Manchester Police confirmed that a child is currently in hospital and that the family is aware of the situation. No further details about the child's condition or the nature of the medical emergency have been released.

Cosy Toes nursery is part of a chain operating four nurseries across Middleton, providing daycare for children up to five years old. The nursery has been approached for comment regarding the incident.

articles.title: Rochdale Borough Council awards contract for homeless family support services
articles.excerpt: The Bond Board Limited has been awarded a contract to manage the Homeless Family Leasing Scheme in Rochdale, providing essential support to families in temporary accommodation.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has awarded a contract for the management and support services of the Homeless Family Leasing Scheme (HFLS) to The Bond Board Limited.

This contract, published on Find a Tender, aims to provide essential tenancy management and support services for homeless families placed in temporary accommodation.

The HFLS will manage approximately 40 leased properties, ensuring that families receive the necessary support to sustain their tenancies. Services will include property management, tenancy sustainment, and move-on support, which are crucial for helping families transition to permanent housing.

This initiative is significant for the local community as it addresses the pressing issue of homelessness in Rochdale. By providing structured support, the council aims to improve the living conditions of vulnerable families and reduce the number of families experiencing homelessness in the borough.

The Bond Board Limited is expected to begin its services shortly, although specific timelines for the implementation of the HFLS have not been disclosed. This development highlights the council's commitment to tackling homelessness and supporting families in need.

articles.title: Eighth arrest in property damage investigation covering Rochdale
articles.excerpt: GMP says Rochdale is among six areas where properties were damaged during October. A 29-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage.
articles.content_html:
An investigation into damage to properties in Rochdale and five other Greater Manchester areas has led to an eighth arrest, police have said.

A 29-year-old man was arrested on Monday morning, 2 November, on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage. Greater Manchester Police said he was being questioned in connection with damage caused during October.

The force said the wider investigation concerns houses in multiple occupation, known as HMOs, and properties mistaken for HMOs.

Since 5 October, police have been made aware of damage to buildings in Rochdale, Salford, Tameside, Stockport, Bolton and Wigan. The latest release does not identify the Rochdale properties or give a separate total for the borough.

GMP said the arrest brought the number of people detained during the investigation to eight. GMP has not given the location of the latest arrest.

Enquiries are continuing. Anyone with information that could help the investigation can contact police on 101 or report it online at https://www.gmp.police.uk/.

Information can also be passed anonymously to the independent charity Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

The arrest is not a finding of guilt. The man is presumed innocent unless and until convicted.

He is one of nine defendants accused of being involved in the abuse orchestrated by the woman's husband, who is in his 60s and from Stockport.

The husband, who cannot be named to protect the victim's identity, is alleged to have subjected his wife to years of abuse while she was unconscious or asleep.

During the opening of the prosecution case on November 2, Louise Oakley KC outlined the disturbing allegations against the husband, stating that he had taken advantage of his wife's intoxication and later escalated to drugging her without her knowledge.

The prosecution claims that over a 20-year period, the husband filmed and shared the abuse with other men, who are also implicated in the case.

The woman was reportedly unaware of the abuse until police arrived at her home last year to arrest her husband. Townsend is accused of assault by penetration, a charge he denies.

The trial has drawn significant attention due to the serious nature of the allegations and the number of defendants involved.

As the trial progresses, it highlights the ongoing issues of domestic abuse and the complexities surrounding consent and accountability.

articles.title: Rochdale driver jailed for 16 months after dangerous police pursuit
articles.excerpt: Bilal Ishaq admitted four driving offences after a pursuit through Rochdale. Police say he ran red lights and twice tried to reverse into pursuing vehicles.
articles.content_html:
A disqualified driver who fled police through Rochdale has been jailed for 16 months and banned from driving for five years.

Bilal Ishaq, 34, of Hey Street, Rochdale, pleaded guilty to dangerous driving, driving while disqualified, failing to stop and driving without insurance, Greater Manchester Police said in a release issued on 2 November.

Officers had tried to stop a vehicle on Foxholes Road in September. GMP said the vehicle was linked to suspected drug dealing. The offences set out in the force’s sentencing announcement were driving offences.

Ishaq drove away, beginning a pursuit through the town. According to police, he reached speeds more than three times the limit, went through red lights and drove on the wrong side of the road.

The force said he also tried to reverse into pursuing police vehicles on two occasions. After crashing, he attempted to run away but was detained by officers.

GMP said Ishaq was already subject to two driving disqualifications imposed in January 2026 following a separate dangerous driving incident in December 2025.

PC Matt Balkwell, from the force’s Motorcycle Unit, said: “His actions could easily have resulted in serious injury or loss of life.”

The officer praised the work of those involved in detaining Ishaq and said police would continue to pursue drivers who endangered their communities.

Scheduled for the weekend of November 12-13, the Ale Trail invites locals and visitors alike to gather friends and embark on a fun social experience. Limited-edition T-shirts will be available for those who complete the trail, adding an extra incentive for participants.

This initiative not only enhances the enjoyment of the event but also supports local businesses in the hospitality sector.

articles.title: Rochdale to review future primary and secondary school place needs on 24 November
articles.excerpt: The council's forward plan schedules reports on primary places through 2030 and secondary places through 2031, alongside high-needs investment, for its 24 November cabinet meeting.
articles.content_html:
How many school places will Rochdale need in the next few years? The borough council has scheduled separate reports on primary and secondary capacity for consideration by its cabinet on Tuesday, 24 November 2026.

The council's official forward plan lists 'Need for Primary School Places 2027–2030' and 'Need for Secondary School Places 2027–2031'. Both are assigned to lead officer Fay Davies and marked as open rather than exempt items. The same meeting is due to consider a 'High Needs Capital and Investment 2026' report, which is marked part exempt because of financial or commercially sensitive information.

These are proposed decision dates, not announcements of new schools, closures, catchment changes or a confirmed number of places. The forward plan identifies subjects the council expects to consider, but it does not itself contain the detailed forecasts, recommendations or decisions. Those must be checked in the published agenda papers when available.

The timing matters to parents thinking ahead to admissions in 2027 and beyond. School-place planning looks at the capacity required across future years, while an individual child's application and allocation follow the separate admissions process. The council's published secondary-school application deadline for September 2027 entry was Saturday, 31 October 2026; families who missed it should use the council's admissions guidance rather than assuming the forthcoming cabinet report changes the deadline.

Other open items listed for 24 November include additional highway maintenance funding, a community asset transfer policy and the calculation of the 2027/28 Council Tax base. The plan also schedules a capital programme for consultation and discretionary fees and charges for consultation for 30 November, with the borough Local Plan publication plan listed for 17 December. These dates can change and do not establish that any proposal has been approved.

Rochdale Daily will check the agenda and published reports before reporting any school-place figures, recommended changes or financial commitments. Residents can read the official forward plan and subsequent meeting papers through the council's democratic services website.

Primary source: Rochdale Borough Council, Notice of Key Decisions and Private Items, 1 October 2026 to 31 January 2027: https://democracy.rochdale.gov.uk/mgListPlanItems.aspx?PlanId=1453.

articles.title: Sandbrook Way KFC licence now permits late-night service until 5am
articles.excerpt: Rochdale's public licensing register shows updated permission for late-night refreshment at the Sandbrook Way KFC, with the restaurant area due to close at midnight under a licence condition.
articles.content_html:
The KFC at Sandbrook Way, Edinburgh Way, Rochdale, has a premises licence permitting late-night refreshment until 5am on every day of the week, according to Rochdale Borough Council's public licensing register.

The register identifies the premises as KFC, OL11 1RY, and names Chicken Cabins Ltd trading as KFC as the licence holder. It lists licence PL(N)1021 with an effective date of 17 October 2026. The permitted premises hours are shown as 10am to 5am, while late-night refreshment is authorised from 11pm to 5am, indoors and outdoors.

There is an important distinction between the permission and what customers can expect on any particular night. The licence sets out what is legally authorised; it is not a verified announcement that every service is operating throughout those hours. A condition in the published record says the restaurant area is to close at midnight, with delivery and drive-through service afterwards.

An earlier version of the same council record, viewed as at 11 October 2026, listed midnight closing on most days and 1am on Friday and Saturday. The updated register therefore records a materially later authorised finish time. It does not explain the commercial reasons for the change or give a launch date for extended service.

The licence includes conditions covering CCTV, door supervision during late-night licensing hours, management of noise and litter, and requests for customers to leave quietly. These are licence requirements, not evidence of a specific incident at the premises.

Customers wanting to know whether collection, drive-through or delivery is currently available after midnight should check directly with the restaurant. Rochdale Daily will update this report if the operator confirms its actual trading timetable.

articles.title: Free play sessions for young children in Littleborough and Middleton this week
articles.excerpt: Littleborough Library has a free under-fives session on Tuesday 3 November, while Junction Library in Middleton is advertising Saturday Lego and Duplo play for children aged two and over.
articles.content_html:
Families looking for free activities with young children this week have two council-listed library sessions to consider in Littleborough and Middleton, with no advance booking required for either.

Littleborough Library, at Hare Hill Park, OL15 9HE, is advertising Library Time for Tuesday, 3 November 2026, from 9.15am to 10.15am. The session is aimed at children under five with their parents, carers or childminders. It offers toys, puppets, simple crafts and a chance to meet other families. The council describes Library Time as an every-other-Tuesday activity, and says visitors can simply turn up.

In Middleton, Junction Library on Grimshaw Lane, M24 2BW, is advertising Lego and Duplo play on Saturday, 7 November, from 10am until noon. It is a free weekly activity for families with children aged two and over. No booking is needed. The council explains that it is informal creative play rather than a structured Lego class; children can choose to have their creations displayed at the library.

The two sessions serve different age groups and take place on different days. Parents should check the council's current event listings before travelling, particularly if a session is affected by an unexpected change to library opening or staffing.

The libraries also offer books and other reading activities, and the council maintains a wider events directory for families who cannot attend either session. A free library session does not require families to buy materials or tickets for the activities described above.

articles.title: Littleborough Christmas lights: Church Street restrictions confirmed for 28 November
articles.excerpt: Church Street restrictions are planned for Littleborough's Christmas lights event on Saturday 28 November, including a daytime waiting ban and an afternoon road closure.
articles.content_html:
Drivers and visitors heading into Littleborough for the Christmas lights event on Saturday, 28 November 2026 should plan around temporary restrictions on Church Street.

Rochdale Borough Council's published traffic notice says a road closure will operate from 1.30pm until 7pm. A prohibition on waiting is due to run from noon until 7pm on the same day, meaning parking arrangements will change before the road closure starts.

The notice identifies Church Street and Peel Street as the location of the restriction. Its wording for the precise starting junction is unclear, because it describes Church Street as beginning at a junction with Church Street itself. Residents who need access to a particular property should check the official notice and seek clarification from the council rather than relying on an assumed boundary.

The council lists Church Street, Morgan Street, Peel Street and Station Road as the alternative route. Drivers should follow temporary signs on the day, as the published notice does not provide a street-by-street map of how each turning will operate.

The restrictions are for the Littleborough Christmas Lights Event 2026, which the council has confirmed for Saturday, 28 November. The traffic notice does not give the entertainment timetable or the exact time of the lights switch-on, so those details should not be assumed from the road closure hours.

Anyone planning to visit shops, businesses or homes around the affected streets should allow extra time, particularly during the afternoon and early evening. Those with deliveries or access requirements may wish to confirm arrangements ahead of the event.

The full council notice, including the restriction wording and alternative route, can be checked at https://www.rochdale.gov.uk/directory-record/2626/littleborough-christmas-lights-event-2026-road-closures-in-littleborough-on-28-november-2026.

articles.title: Rochdale reception school applications for 2027: deadline, preferences and offer dates
articles.excerpt: Parents applying for a Rochdale borough reception place starting September 2027 have until 15 January. The council has also confirmed the offer date and rules for school preferences.
articles.content_html:
Applications for reception places at Rochdale borough primary schools for September 2027 are open, with parents and carers given until Friday, 15 January 2027 to apply on time.

Rochdale Borough Council opened its online admissions system on 14 September 2026. The council says parents should submit their application before the January closing date; otherwise, it will be treated as late. National offer day for reception places is Friday, 16 April 2027, when families can find out which school has been offered.

Parents are encouraged to name five different schools in their order of preference. Listing only one school does not improve the chance of being offered that school. If it is oversubscribed, the published admissions criteria are applied; where a preferred school cannot be offered, the council considers the other preferences and available places.

The council advises families to check each school's admissions policy before applying. The rules for community and voluntary controlled schools are not necessarily the same as those for academies, foundation or voluntary aided schools. Attending a school's nursery class does not normally guarantee priority for its reception class. Some schools also ask parents to submit supplementary forms directly to the school.

For families who move house after applying, the council lists Friday, 12 February 2027 as the final date for address changes to be considered in the initial allocation, subject to the required evidence. Changes of school preference after the application deadline are treated as late.

Parents considering deferring their child's start should still apply by 15 January. The council explains that the rules depend on the child's birthday, and applications for a place outside the normal age group require supporting evidence and an individual decision by the admission authority.

Children living in Rochdale borough apply through Rochdale Borough Council even when choosing a school outside the borough. Families who live elsewhere must apply through their own council. The school admissions team can be contacted at school.admissions@rochdale.gov.uk or 0300 303 0340.

Full dates, admissions guidance and the application route are published at https://www.rochdale.gov.uk/school-admissions-appeals/apply-primary-school-place. Families can also consult the council's guidance before choosing schools at https://www.rochdale.gov.uk/school-admissions-appeals/apply-primary-school-place/3.

articles.title: Rochdale Borough Council awards ABEN hostel accommodation contracts
articles.excerpt: The Sanctuary Trust Limited and Stepping Stone Projects have been awarded contracts to provide supported accommodation for homeless individuals in Rochdale.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has awarded two contracts under the A Bed for Every Night (ABEN) scheme to provide supported accommodation for individuals who are homeless or at risk of rough sleeping.

The contracts were awarded to The Sanctuary Trust Limited and Stepping Stone Projects, as announced on November 2, 2026.

The Sanctuary Trust Limited will deliver approximately 20 units of HMO-style supported accommodation, which includes accommodation management, support planning, and tenancy sustainment. This initiative aims to assist individuals in transitioning from homelessness to stable housing.

Meanwhile, Stepping Stone Projects has been awarded a contract to provide around 34 units of dispersed accommodation, specifically aimed at helping women move towards stable accommodation and independence. This service will also include housing-related support services.

These contracts are part of Rochdale's ongoing efforts to address homelessness in the area, ensuring that vulnerable individuals receive the necessary support and accommodation.

The implementation of these services is expected to have a significant positive impact on the local community by providing essential resources for those in need.

articles.title: Rochdale Council approves new Storage World building in Middleton
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Council has approved plans for a new Storage World building in Middleton, following a fire that destroyed the previous structure.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Council has approved the rebuilding of Storage World in Middleton town centre. The planning application submitted by Self-Storage Performance Management International Ltd (SSPMI) was greenlit to replace the building on Old Hall Street, which was destroyed by fire in June last year.

The new development will be a £12 million mixed-use building, smaller in footprint but taller than the previous structure.

It will feature self-storage units on the upper floors and commercial units on the ground floor, occupying half the space of the former Storage World but with two additional storeys to maintain capacity.

In their application, P4 Planning highlighted the aim to create a modern design that would not only restore self-storage services but also stimulate small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) activity in the area.

They noted that the design would reflect the historical context of the site, which previously housed Albany Mill until 1975.

This development is expected to contribute positively to the regeneration of Middleton town centre, enhancing the local economy and providing much-needed facilities for residents and businesses alike.

articles.title: Mark Winstanley returns to stage after MS diagnosis for Rochdale comedy show
articles.excerpt: Actor Mark Winstanley will perform in 'Cabaret Schmabaret' at the Ukrainian Centre on 19 November, marking his return to the stage after a five-year hiatus due to multiple sclerosis.
articles.content_html:
Actor Mark Winstanley is set to return to the stage after a five-year break following his diagnosis with multiple sclerosis. He will perform in 'Cabaret Schmabaret' at the Ukrainian Centre in Rochdale on 19 November, bringing his comedic talents back to the local audience.

Winstanley, who co-runs the Manchester-based theatre company The Performers’ Playground with Alice Robinson, has a rich history in theatre, having performed nationally and internationally with various touring companies.

His return is particularly significant as it showcases his resilience and commitment to the arts despite his health challenges.

In addition to 'Cabaret Schmabaret', The Performers’ Playground is also fundraising for a separate production of 'Ubu Royale', which is currently in research and development. This production is designed to accommodate Winstanley's mobility and fatigue issues, with plans for a national tour in 2027.

Winstanley's comeback not only highlights his personal journey but also serves as an inspiration for others facing similar challenges. Local audiences can look forward to enjoying a unique comedic experience while supporting a talented artist's return to the stage.

The project is in research and development, with plans to share the work this year before a proposed national tour in 2027. Ubu Royale is Neil Bartlett’s translation of Alfred Jarry’s Ubu Roi . It follows Pa Ubu and Ma Ubu, two would-be monarchs whose pursuit of power leads to chaos. The production will feature three performers playing more than 20 characters, using puppetry and a set built from discarded materials and repurposed mobility aids. The company describes it as its most ambitious project to date, combining satire and physical comedy with frequent strong language and bodily humour. Alongside Mark, the cast and creative team includes Susanna Amato, David Nixon, Alice Robinson, Thomas Toppler and Sophie Tyrrell. Mark, Alice, Susanna and David also work as practitioners and teachers. Their collective experience includes work across RADA, Performers College, Ecole Philippe Gaulier, Contact, Cheshire Dance, Uncurbed Collective, Handmade Parade and Driftwood Studio. The team hopes to develop skills in performance, movement, theatre-making, puppetry, mobility and access that they can share with students and other artists. “We want accessibility to be part of the creative process from the very beginning, not something added afterwards. By exploring how ambitious theatre can be made around Mark's access needs, we hope to develop approaches that can benefit not only this production, but the performers and theatre-makers who come after it.” Donations will help fund the production, support its artists and provide the access arrangements needed to make the work possible. articles.title: Missed the secondary school deadline in Rochdale? What parents need to do next
articles.excerpt: Rochdale's 31 October deadline has passed, but families can still apply for a Year 7 place for September 2027. Here is how late applications are handled and when offers are expected.
articles.content_html:
Families who missed Rochdale borough's secondary school application deadline can still submit an application for a Year 7 place starting in September 2027. The council's closing date was Saturday, 31 October 2026, but its online Parent Portal remains the route for late applications.

The important difference is when the application will be considered. Rochdale Borough Council says applications received after the deadline are not processed until after national offer day on Monday, 1 March 2027, because applications submitted on time take priority. Schools do not reserve places for late applicants, so a preferred school may already be full when a late application is assessed.

Parents are advised to list all five school preferences, rather than naming only one school. The council uses its normal published admissions criteria to allocate places remaining after the on-time round. Naming a single preference does not increase the chance of securing that school.

For late applications made before 1 March 2027, the council aims to issue an offer by Friday, 30 April 2027. Applications made from 1 March to 19 March are expected to receive an offer by Friday, 7 May. Applications submitted after 19 March are handled on a later timetable set out in the council's admissions guidance. These are target dates, not guarantees of a particular school.

Children who live in Rochdale borough must apply through Rochdale Borough Council even if a preferred school is outside the borough. Families living in another local authority area should apply through their home council, including any Rochdale schools among their preferences. Some faith schools and academies may require supplementary evidence, which must be supplied to the school itself.

Parents should keep the email confirming submission. The council advises applicants to resubmit their form after making changes in the Parent Portal. Families needing help can contact the school admissions team at school.admissions@rochdale.gov.uk or 0300 303 0340, Monday to Friday, 9am to 4.45pm.

The council's current application instructions, late-offer timetable and Parent Portal link are at https://www.rochdale.gov.uk/school-admissions-appeals/apply-secondary-school-place/4.

articles.title: Middleton care worker celebrated after 27 years at Langfield Care Home
articles.excerpt: Karen Haycock, who joined Langfield Care Home in Langley in May 1999, was surprised by colleagues and residents marking what the home calls 10,000 days of service.
articles.content_html:
A support worker at a Middleton care home has been celebrated by colleagues and residents after more than 27 years of looking after people at the home.

Karen Haycock, a specialist support worker at Langfield Care Home on Wood Street, Langley, was surprised with gifts, flowers and cards at a gathering on 27 October.

The home is marking the occasion as 10,000 days of service. Karen joined the home’s operator, Orchard Healthcare Group, in May 1999 — roughly 10,000 days ago — so the milestone reflects the length of her time with the home rather than a count of individual shifts.

Over her career Karen has worked across residential care, dementia care and nursing. She now works in the home’s Reconnect dementia community, which supports residents living with advanced dementia.

Along the way she completed an NVQ Level 2, took part in Orchard’s Step Up programme and undertook specialist Dementia Promise training. The group says she has seen the sector change considerably in that time, with better specialist training, equipment and more individual approaches to caring for people with dementia.

For Karen, though, the job is still about people. “I love spending time with the residents. They become your family,” she said.

Asked what she would tell anyone thinking about a career in care, she said: “You need to give it 100% to be able to make a difference to people, and that’s the best part.”

Home manager Lisa-Marie Hutchinson said: “Karen’s 10,000 working days is a fantastic achievement, and we were delighted to celebrate this special milestone with her and show her how much she is appreciated.”

Long service of this kind is increasingly rare in adult social care, where staff turnover is high and many homes rely on a changing workforce. For residents living with dementia, a familiar face who has known the home for decades can make a real difference to day-to-day life and to families choosing care for a relative.

Langfield is one of 23 care homes run by Harrogate-based Orchard Healthcare Group across the North of England and the Midlands. The group says the home holds a Good rating from the Care Quality Commission.
